q: 1. Segregation in concrete results in
explain: Segregation separates coarse aggregate, mortar, and water unevenly, which can cause honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling all at once depending on where separation occurs.

q: 2. Minimum number of days required for curing fresh laid concrete under normal atmospheric condition is
explain: Under normal atmospheric conditions, a minimum curing period of 7 days is generally specified to allow adequate hydration and strength gain of concrete.

q: 3. Horizontal construction joint in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls can be provided at any of these convenient locations — soffit, floor, or window sill level — depending on the pour sequence, so all apply.

q: 4. In transportation of concrete by pumps
options: the slump should not be less than 50 mm and more than 80mm
the water cement ratio should remain between 0.5 to 0.65
the number of bends in a pipe line should be as small as possible
explain: Successful pumping of concrete requires appropriate slump range, controlled water-cement ratio, and minimizing pipeline bends to reduce friction losses, so all conditions apply together.

q: 5. 1% of voids in concrete mix would reduce its strength by about
explain: As a general rule of thumb used in concrete technology, each 1% of entrapped air voids reduces compressive strength by approximately 5%.

q: 6. After the curing of 28 days, the concrete gains strength upto (As per IS)
explain: By IS convention, 28-day cured concrete is considered to have gained 100% of its designated characteristic (design) strength, though it continues to gain further strength beyond 28 days.

q: 7. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in walls are conveniently located at floor levels, lintel soffit levels, and window sill levels, as these are natural break points in the wall's structural continuity.

q: 8. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient/thorough than machine mixing, an additional 10% cement is recommended to compensate for the loss in mixing efficiency.

q: 9. The construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature across many types of concrete structures including roads, retaining walls, and tunnel linings, wherever concreting must be done in stages.

q: 10. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by a vibrator if it is
explain: Plastic (wet, high-slump) concrete does not need mechanical vibration and is actually unsuitable for it, since vibration can cause segregation and bleeding in already-flowable mixes.

q: 11. The concrete mix which is not amicable for smooth finish is said to posses
explain: A harsh concrete mix — one with excessive hardness/harshness due to insufficient fines or paste — is difficult to finish smoothly.

q: 12. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete, is
explain: Sodium carbonates and bicarbonates present in mixing water can adversely affect the setting time and reduce the strength of concrete.

q: 13. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

q: 14. Which of the following types of concrete mixers is most commonly used in precast concrete factories?
explain: Pan type mixers, which provide intensive and uniform mixing suited to stiff/low-slump mixes, are most commonly used in precast concrete factory production.

q: 15. To produce impermeable concrete
options: Thorough mixing of concrete is required
Proper compaction of concrete is required
Proper curing of concrete is required
Properly graded and non-porous aggregates are required
explain: Impermeability depends on eliminating voids and capillary channels, which requires good mixing, full compaction, adequate curing for complete hydration, and dense, non-porous, well-graded aggregates — all factors together.

q: 16. For concreting tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete in confined and elongated spaces like tunnel linings, where other methods are impractical.

q: 17. Transport of concrete by pumps, is done for a distance of
explain: Concrete pumps are capable of effectively transporting concrete over distances of up to about 400m through pipelines.

q: 18. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs, is done by
explain: For flat horizontal surfaces like pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, ponding (creating a shallow water layer over the surface) is the commonly used curing method.

q: 19. Curing a concrete for long period ensures better
explain: Extended curing periods allow more complete hydration, which improves volume stability, strength, water-tightness, and overall durability of concrete all together.

q: 20. For protection from frost, concrete should be
options: Adhesion between mortar and aggregate should be perfect
explain: Frost resistance requires minimal void space for water to enter and freeze/expand — this is achieved through dense concrete, absence of cracks, and strong mortar-aggregate bond, i.e., all of the above together.

q: 21. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
explain: Trowelling is the final finishing operation performed on a concrete floor surface to achieve a smooth, dense, and polished finish.

q: 22. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
explain: Expansion joints are typically provided in long concrete structures once the length exceeds about 45m, to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction movements.

q: 23. For preparing a test-specimen, it is necessary
options: to mix cement and fine aggregate by dry hand
to mix water to the cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates
to oil inter surface of the mould and the base plate, before placing concrete
explain: All these steps - dry mixing of cement and fine aggregate, mixing in coarse aggregate, adding water, and oiling the mould interior - are standard necessary steps in preparing a proper concrete test specimen.

q: 24. The concrete may achieve 100% strength after
explain: While 28-day strength is used as the standard design reference, concrete continues to gain strength gradually and may reach close to its full/ultimate strength after about 1 year of curing.

q: 25. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
explain: Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions in freshly placed concrete to allow proper hydration and strength development.

q: 26. While compacting the concrete by mechanical vibrator, slump should not exceed
explain: For mechanically vibrated concrete, the recommended slump should not exceed about 50 mm, since higher slump/wetter mixes are meant for hand compaction.

q: 27. No shrinkage occurs if the concrete is placed in a relative humidity of
explain: At 100% relative humidity, there is no moisture loss from the concrete to the surrounding environment, so drying shrinkage does not occur.

q: 28. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching ensures the correct mix proportions, which in turn governs the strength, workability, and durability of the resulting concrete — all of these depend on it.

q: 29. Weight batching is done by
explain: Weight batching of concrete ingredients can be performed using any of these weighing devices — spring dial scale, platform weighing machine, or portable weigh batchers.

q: 30. The capacity of concrete mixer is expressed in terms of
options: total volume of concrete produced per day
total volume of concrete produced in 8 hrs
total volume of concrete produced per hr
volume of concrete mix handled per batch
explain: The capacity of a concrete mixer is standardly expressed as the volume of concrete mix it can handle per batch (e.g., a 150-litre mixer, 10/7 mixer, etc.).

q: 31. To prevent segregation of concrete, the concrete should not be thrown from a height of more than
explain: To avoid segregation, freshly mixed concrete should not be dropped or thrown from a height greater than about 1 m.

q: 32. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The weight of ingredients of concrete mix, is taken in kilograms
water and aggregates is measured in liters
the finished concrete is measured in cubic metres
20 bags of cement make one tonne
explain: All these statements are factually correct standard conventions used in concrete work - weight in kg, water/aggregates in litres, finished concrete in cubic metres, and 20 bags of 50 kg cement equal one tonne.

q: 33. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
explain: Concrete placing is preferably carried out at a moderate temperature of around 27 ± 2°C, which is favourable for proper hydration and setting without excessive heat or cold-related issues.

q: 34. To prevent segregation, the maximum vertical height for placing concrete, is
explain: To prevent segregation of concrete during placing (free fall), the maximum vertical drop height allowed is limited to about 150 cm (1.5 m).

q: 35. 'Tremie' is a
explain: A 'tremie' is a water-tight pipe used to place concrete underwater or in deep foundations, preventing the concrete from mixing with water during placement.

q: 36. The drying of concrete after casting results in
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete, the paste loses volume, causing drying shrinkage.

q: 37. Compaction of mechanical vibrations is suitable for
options: all the mixes except very plastic mixes
explain: Mechanical vibration compaction is versatile and suitable across all grades of concrete, all structural elements, and various mix consistencies (except very plastic mixes), making it broadly applicable.

q: 38. A surface vibrator for compaction of concrete is preferred for all of the following except
explain: Surface vibrators, being effective mainly for shallow/thin horizontal sections, are not preferred for columns (which are deep, vertical, heavily reinforced members) unlike footings, slabs, or pavements.

q: 39. Curing
options: prevents the loss of water by evaporation
explain: Curing serves multiple purposes simultaneously - it reduces shrinkage, preserves the desired properties of concrete, and prevents premature loss of moisture through evaporation.

q: 40. Generally curing is allowed only after concreting of
explain: Curing is generally started/allowed after an initial period of about 24 hours from concreting, once the concrete has achieved sufficient initial set to withstand water application without damage.

q: 41. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: there should not be any loss of cement from the charged drum of the mixer
cement should be mixed for at least one minute
10% of water is placed in the rotating drum before adding dry material
10% of water is added after placing the other ingredients in the drum
explain: All these are standard good-practice requirements for charging and mixing a concrete mixer, so the combined statement 'all of the above' is correct.

q: 42. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface, is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete with a straightedge to remove humps and hollows and bring the surface to the required level.

q: 43. The ratio of the length and breadth of wooden float, is
explain: A wooden float used for finishing concrete surfaces typically has a length-to-breadth ratio of about 7.5, giving a long narrow tool for smoothing the surface.

q: 44. Construction joints are provided
options: where BM and SF are small
where it is supported by another member
at 18 m apart in huge structures
in concrete wall at sill level of windows
explain: Construction joints are located at points of low bending moment/shear, at supports, at regular intervals in large structures, and at window sill levels in walls — all of these are valid locations.

q: 45. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: construction joints in columns are provided a few cm below the junction of beam
construction joints in columns are provided at the bottom haunching
construction joints in beam and slabs are provided within middle third
construction joints are generally provided in positions subjected to least shear force
explain: Each statement correctly describes accepted practice for locating construction joints in columns, beams and slabs, so the combined answer 'all of the above' applies.

q: 46. According to the recommendations of IS:456-2000, expansion joints
options: are provided where plane changes abruptly
are provided to ensure minimum resistance
do not carry reinforcement across them
explain: IS:456-2000 recommends expansion joints at abrupt plan changes, designed to offer minimum resistance to movement, supported independently, and without reinforcement crossing them — all points are valid.

q: 47. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature & time
explain: Maturity is a concept that combines the effects of curing temperature and time (the temperature-time factor), used to estimate strength gain, rather than simply age.

q: 48. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete during drying, the paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink.

q: 49. As compared to moist cured concrete, the permeability of steam cured concrete is
explain: Steam curing, due to its accelerated hydration process, tends to produce a coarser pore structure, resulting in higher permeability compared to normally moist-cured concrete.

q: 50. For high degree of workability, the slump value should vary between
explain: As per the slump classification used in this text, a high degree of workability corresponds to a slump value in the range of 80 to 100 mm.

q: 51. Concreting should be stopped when temperature falls below …
explain: Concreting operations are generally stopped once the ambient temperature drops below about 4.5°C, since hydration slows drastically and frost damage risk increases.

q: 52. The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by :
explain: Proper compaction that removes entrapped/excess air from freshly placed concrete has been found to increase its strength by roughly 15 to 20%.
